expectations.text: B1: Gives an honest constraint and a workable option (Linux VM, or utun with limits)
expectations.evidence: States the constraint honestly: 'Native TAP on macOS is basically dead (tuntaposx unmaintained, kext signing issues, Apple Silicon)' and gives workable options with limits: 'use utun for the TCP/IP part (IP/TCP/UDP), and if they specifically need Ethernet/ARP (layer 2), either emulate the wire with a Unix-socket "virtual cable" or run a Linux VM'

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Answer ends mid-outline: '1. Direct answer: Native TAP on macOS: effectively no... 2. Route A: utun' — no closing runnable checkpoint; commands like 'ifconfig utunN 10.0.0.1 10.0.0.2 up' appear mid-text with no expected output/behaviour stated

expectations.text: B3: States TAP/TUN as in the tutorial is Linux-specific and suggests a Linux VM/container
expectations.evidence: 'On Linux, /dev/net/tun gives you TUN/TAP devices natively' plus macOS lacks native TAP, and suggests VM: 'VM-based: run Linux in QEMU/UTM/Multipass/Lima, use real TAP inside the VM. This is the most faithful "TAP" experience'; also 'or just develop in a Linux VM' and Docker-in-VM note

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: '## FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0)' and '## SHELL COMMANDS RUN (0)'; only read-only tool calls (glob, grep) within the workspace; no brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install/gem install commands run or written outside the project
